children: New Delhi, Oct. 18 -- Tata Steel shares | Stock to buy | Q2 Results 2026: Tata Group's flagship metal company has declared the board meeting date on 27 October to announce Q2 results 2026. The company made the board meeting date public through an exchange filing on Friday. The Tata Steel board will consider and approve both Q2FY27 and H1FY27 earnings during the board meeting scheduled on the Q2 results date.

Tata Steel declared the Q2 results 2026 date in an exchange filing on Friday, saying, "A meeting of the Board of Directors of Tata Steel Limited ('Company') will be held on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, inter alia, to consider and take on record the audited Standalone and unaudited Consolidated financial results of the Company for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026."

Highlighting the key factors that the market would track after the announcement of Tata Steel Q2 results 2026, Mahesh M Ojha, VP - Research and Business Development, said, "In Tata Steel's Q2 results 2026, the key factors market participants are likely to track are Indian steel demand, domestic steel prices, European operations, raw-material costs and the company's operating margins." However, he said that Tata Steel is expected to outperform its peers due to the better margin resilience in the September 2026 quarter.

Tata Steel also figures in Nuvama's Q2FY27 metal picks. Based on its Q2 FY27 estimates, Nuvama identifies Coal India and Tata Steel as outperformers, backed by stronger volume growth, e-auction realisations and relatively better margin resilience.

The brokerage expects Tata Steel to also outperform its peers. Its relatively higher exposure to flat steel is likely to limit the impact of the decline in long steel prices, with blended realisation expected to fall by only around Rs.500 to Rs.600 per tonne QoQ. Tata Steel's EBITDA per tonne is estimated to decline by around Rs.610 per tonne, the lowest decline among the steel companies covered by Nuvama.

Nuvama also expects Tata Steel Europe to turn EBITDA-positive, at around $7 per tonne in Q2 from a loss of $17 per tonne in Q1, helped by higher prices and lower costs in the Netherlands. This improvement is likely to be partly offset by higher losses in the UK.

Tata Steel shares finished lower at Rs.175.50 per share on Friday. Tata Steel's share price has corrected over 5% in one month, more than 17% in six months, and around 3.50% in YTD. However, the Tata Group stock has delivered around a 2% return over the past year.

Decoding the technical chart of Tata Steel shares, Mahesh M Ojha of KC Securities said, "Tata Steel shares are looking weak on the technical chart, but a trend reversal is visible around the current support zone of Rs.172 to Rs.170 per share. The stock is facing a hurdle in the Rs.180 to Rs.181 band. On breaking above this resistance on a closing basis, we can expect the Tata Steel share price to touch the upside target of Rs.196 apiece."

Ojha said that existing Tata Steel shareholders should hold the scrip, maintaining the stop-loss at Rs.168 for the upside target of Rs.196. He said that fresh investors can also buy Tata Steel stock at around Rs.175, with a short-term target of Rs.196, maintaining a strict stop-loss at Rs.168.
